reason: Run and operation events of deleted records are pruned. Migration 0018 replaces the unconditional no-delete triggers on run_events and operation_events (SQLite and PostgreSQL) with owner-aware ones: updates stay refused, a delete is refused while the owning record (run_id's Mission/chat turn/harness turn; the project, and the operation_id's record for listed kinds) exists. Deleting a conversation, Mission, archived project or single owning record hands the ids to a background purger that deletes their history in paused 1,000-row batches; Core prunes older leftovers at startup; the CLI gains maintenance prune-events and maintenance vacuum. tests/v3/test_event_history_retention.py covers the triggers, mapping, batched and idempotent prune, settle age and stop, the four delete paths, the deferred purge, terminal audit and export after a prune, the startup prune and vacuum. tests/v3/test_migrations.py (also on PostgreSQL in the database-migrations job) covers upgrade/downgrade of 0018 and the prune on each dialect. The other files cover the delete paths (storage, guarded delete, archived project deletion, temporary chat, chat API, browser research/assessment deletes), the readers of kept history (terminal history and container terminal replay, doctor, exporter, session state, approval continuation, harness activity, report sign-off, operators) and the Core lifespan beside unreadable rows.
exclusions: Full suites are not approved and are excluded. No UI, native or Playwright code changes: the operator surfaces are unchanged (a deleted conversation already disappeared from the UI; its stored history now goes too), so frontend, native and Playwright selections are empty. Provider, harness adapter, Mission orchestration and chat routing code is unchanged and not selected; their event writers were only read to map event ownership. test_executions/test_execution_ai are not selected: execution events are only removed after their execution is deleted, which the retention tests cover at the storage layer.
